candidate_atomics.description: Extend the existing dangerous-command regex guard so wildcard gaps are evaluated across newline characters, preventing shell-continuation input from bypassing the established approval and blocking path. The pattern catalog, detector result tuple, approval policy, and terminal-tool call-site contract remain unchanged.
candidate_atomics.name: newline-aware-dangerous-pattern-guard

semantic_action.intent: Prevent a dangerous command from being classified as safe solely because a newline separates tokens that an existing .* regex pattern is intended to connect.
parameters: existing dangerous-command regex patterns containing wildcard gaps
detector result tuple of dangerous status, pattern key, and description
semantic_action.post_state: The existing pattern list is searched with both case-insensitive and DOTALL semantics, so .* spans newline characters; representative line-split curl, wget, dd, and chmod commands reach the dangerous result while the downstream approval/blocking interface remains unchanged.
semantic_action.pre_state: The detector lowercased the command and called regex search with only re.IGNORECASE. Patterns containing .* therefore stopped at newline characters, allowing line-split dangerous commands to evade classification and never enter the normal dangerous-command approval path.
semantic_action.validation: The four regression cases added in the pinned change assert is_dangerous is True for newline-separated curl-to-shell, wget-to-shell, dd, and recursive-chmod commands. The pinned PR states that all four fail without the flag and that all 33 tests pass with it.

candidate_atomics.description: Add focused regression coverage for the multiline boundary across the dangerous pattern families named by the issue, making the security invariant independently testable and preventing a future removal of newline-aware matching.
candidate_atomics.name: multiline-dangerous-command-regression-coverage

semantic_action.intent: Lock in the invariant that inserting a shell line break between dangerous command fragments does not turn the detector result into safe.
parameters: newline-separated curl and wget pipeline fixtures
semantic_action.post_state: The test suite contains a TestMultilineBypass group with four cases, and each case asserts that the detector returns True for the corresponding line-split command.
semantic_action.pre_state: The parent test file covered single-line dangerous commands and existing false-positive cases but had no dedicated assertions for newline-separated command fragments.
semantic_action.validation: The pinned PR description states that all four new multiline tests fail without the implementation change and that all 33 tests in the scoped test file pass with it.

candidate_workflows.description: Use this workflow when a security classifier relies on regex wildcard gaps while accepting command text that may contain line breaks or shell continuations. Preserve the existing dangerous-pattern catalog, detector return shape, approval modes, terminal call site, and explicit force behavior; do not replace the guard with a shell parser or broaden unrelated policy rules.
candidate_workflows.name: close-multiline-dangerous-command-detection-gap

workflow_graph.entry_state: The dangerous-command detector uses patterns whose wildcard portions do not span newline characters, and the test suite lacks line-split representatives for the affected command forms.
workflow_graph.exit_state: The same approval guard classifies the four representative multiline dangerous commands as dangerous before ordinary execution handling, the existing result and caller contracts remain intact, and the pinned PR reports the scoped tests passing.
workflow_graph.goal: Ensure newline-bearing command text cannot bypass dangerous-command detection because a wildcard stops at a line break.
unresolved_or_deferred: The pinned change establishes coverage for four representative multiline patterns; it does not establish complete protection against every shell obfuscation or syntax-normalization technique.

episode.after: At pinned implementation ref 7166647ca132d54149af35dfd21312a1e3c19625, tools/approval.py still lowercases the command and iterates over the same DANGEROUS_PATTERNS list, but re.search now uses re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL. The four added TestMultilineBypass cases assert that line-split curl-to-shell, wget-to-shell, dd, and recursive-chmod commands are dangerous. The terminal tool continues to delegate through the same approval function and returns approval_required or blocked before command preparation when the guard denies execution.
episode.before: At parent/base ref 7b23dbfe6841002328f96e8d97980e1d11410db5, detect_dangerous_command lowercased the input and called re.search(pattern, command_lower, re.IGNORECASE) only. Several existing dangerous patterns used .* to connect command fragments, so the regular-expression dot stopped at newline characters. A shell-continuation command could therefore be reported as non-dangerous and fail to enter the existing approval or blocking path used by the terminal tool.
episode.diff: The pinned commit changes exactly two files. In tools/approval.py it makes a one-line behavioral change, adding re.DOTALL to the existing re.IGNORECASE search flags. In tests/tools/test_approval.py it adds 24 lines containing the TestMultilineBypass class and four regression tests. The compare metadata reports 25 additions and 1 deletion overall; no terminal-tool call site or approval-result contract is changed.
episode.title: Prevent newline-based bypasses in dangerous command detection

evidence_units.claim: Issue #232 identifies a bypass in which newline-containing shell-continuation commands evade patterns such as curl or wget piped to a shell, dd with an if= operand, and recursive chmod with 777 because the detector uses .* without DOTALL.
The parent state at 7b23dbfe6841002328f96e8d97980e1d11410db5 contains the pre-fix detector call re.search(pattern, command_lower, re.IGNORECASE), with no DOTALL flag.

The pinned implementation retains dangerous patterns whose intended multi-token matches contain .*, including recursive chmod followed by 777, dd followed by if=, remote curl or wget piped to a shell, xargs with rm, and find patterns.

Commit 7166647ca132d54149af35dfd21312a1e3c19625 is titled fix(security): add re.DOTALL to prevent multiline bypass of dangerous command detection and contains the one-line flag change plus four multiline regression tests.

The parent-to-head comparison identifies parent 7b23dbfe6841002328f96e8d97980e1d11410db5, one commit, and exactly two modified files: tools/approval.py and tests/tools/test_approval.py, with 24 test additions and a one-line implementation replacement.

At the pinned ref, tools/terminal_tool.py imports the centralized dangerous-command implementation and delegates _check_dangerous_command(command, env_type) to it while passing the existing approval callback.

At the pinned ref, the terminal tool invokes the dangerous-command check when force is false and returns approval_required or blocked responses before preparing the command for execution when approval is not granted.
The parent test file contains existing single-line dangerous-command tests and ends after the existing recursive-delete cases; it has no TestMultilineBypass group or newline-specific assertions.

The pinned test file adds TestMultilineBypass with four assertions that is_dangerous is True for curl followed by a newline and | sh, wget followed by a newline and | bash, dd followed by a newline and if=, and chmod --recursive followed by a newline and 777.
PR #233 identifies the pinned head SHA, states that all four new tests fail without the fix, and reports that all 33 tests pass with the fix.

unresolved_questions: The pinned change establishes coverage for four representative newline-based bypasses, but it does not establish complete coverage for every shell obfuscation, quoting form, or multiline syntax that could affect a regex-based command classifier.
